files.fileContent:
# PostHog Analytics — TWO projects, two keys, on purpose.
#
# The website and the iOS app are separate products with separate north stars,
# so they have separate PostHog projects. This repo talks to both.
#
# Browser SDK (src/instrumentation-client.ts, via the /ingest reverse proxy) →
# the WEBSITE project. Marketing traffic and App Store handoffs.
NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY=
#
# Server-side client (src/lib/analytics/server.ts) → the iOS APP project.
# /api/identify and /api/diagnose are only ever called by the app, so
# scan_completed / scan_failed are product events and belong next to the rest
# of that user's journey. Server-only and NOT NEXT_PUBLIC_: the old gate was
# the public key, which Next inlines at build time and which is not guaranteed
# present in the server runtime — that is why these events sent nothing for
# 90 days.
POSTHOG_APP_KEY=
#
# The EU host is hardcoded in both — there is no host env var.

# Sentry. All three runtimes (browser/server/edge) use the public DSN;
# SENTRY_DSN optionally overrides it for the server/edge inits only.
# SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN is a BUILD-time secret (set it on the Railway service, not
# here) — it enables source-map upload; without it prod stack traces stay
# minified. Release tagging comes from RAILWAY_GIT_COMMIT_SHA automatically.
NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=
SENTRY_DSN=

# App Store
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_STORE_URL=
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_STORE_ID=
# Apple provider ID, the `pt` in a campaign link. It is NOT displayed anywhere
# to look up — Apple generates it the first time you create a campaign link,
# and it is then static forever. App Store Connect → Apps → the app →
# Analytics → Acquisition → Campaigns → (+). Create one campaign, then read
# the pt= value off the link Apple hands back. (The + only appears once the app
# has analytics data.)
#
# This is what closes the web-to-install loop: DownloadButton appends
# ?pt=…&ct=web-<placement>&mt=8, and App Store Connect then reports installs
# per website surface under Analytics → Sources → Campaigns. PostHog cannot
# follow a visitor across the App Store boundary, so without this the north
# star has no quality guardrail. Unset → plain App Store links, nothing breaks.
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_STORE_PROVIDER_TOKEN=

# RevenueCat Web Billing
# Public SDK key for fetching offerings (used by /pricing display).
# Currently issued only as a sandbox key — that's fine for read-only price display.
NEXT_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_API_KEY=

# Firebase Admin (server-only — required for App Check token verification on /api/identify and /api/diagnose).
# Pull from Firebase Console → Project Settings → Service Accounts → Generate new private key.
# FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID must match the iOS app's GoogleService-Info.plist PROJECT_ID.
# FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY should be the PEM with \n-escaped newlines (e.g. "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\n").
FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=
FIREBASE_CLIENT_EMAIL=
FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY=

# Optional comma-separated allow-list of App Check app IDs. verifyToken only
# proves a token was minted for SOME app in the Firebase project; set this to
# the known iOS app's App ID(s) to reject tokens from any other app or a leaked
# debug token. Unset → any app in the project is accepted.
APPCHECK_ALLOWED_APP_IDS=

# Extra exact hostnames (comma-separated) allowed to appear in /api/posts feed
# URLs, beyond the production host (derived from NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL) and
# localhost. A staging deploy sets its own Railway host here; leave blank in
# production. Prevents a spoofed x-forwarded-host from poisoning the cached feed.
POSTS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=

# Environment name (also the Sentry environment). Provider selection keys off
# this: APP_ENV=production wires the real identify/diagnose vendors; any other
# value (unset, development, staging) serves hardcoded mock responses so UI
# iteration never spends Kindwise credits or OpenAI diagnose tokens.
APP_ENV=

# The browser's copy of APP_ENV. Next inlines ONLY the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix into
# the client bundle, so APP_ENV is undefined in the browser no matter how it is
# set on Railway — the trap that tagged every browser Sentry event
# "environment: development", production included, for months (see
# docs/monitoring.md, 2026-08-12). Set it to the same value as APP_ENV.
#
# PostHog registers this as a super property on every event, and the website
# north-star tiles filter on `environment = production`. Without it, staging
# traffic and your own testing inflate Weekly App Store Handoffs. Falls back to
# NODE_ENV when unset, so local dev labels itself "development" rather than
# quietly counting as production.
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=

# AI provider (server-only) — powers /api/identify, /api/diagnose, and care content generation.
# Provider can be swapped by editing src/lib/ai/index.ts only; no other files reference it.
# Issue a project-scoped key in the provider dashboard. Set a prepaid balance and a hard
# monthly limit — that limit is the cost cap.
AI_API_KEY=
# Optional override of the default model.
AI_MODEL=

# Kindwise (Plant.id) — the runtime identify provider when APP_ENV=production
# (gated at 0.50, OpenAI as the credit-exhaustion fallback). Bills one prepaid
# credit per image. Also scored by the evals/ harness.
KINDWISE_API_KEY=
# Optional overrides of environment-based provider selection. Values:
# identify: kindwise | openai | mock; diagnose: openai | mock. Setting
# IDENTIFY_PROVIDER=kindwise locally is the lever for a deliberate real call.
IDENTIFY_PROVIDER=
DIAGNOSE_PROVIDER=

# Per-uid MONTHLY scan ceiling (on top of the 10s cooldown) — the cumulative
# cost cap. Defaults 40 / 80; sized so a €5/mo sub stays margin-positive at
# ~€0.055/identify under either App Store cut. Resets at the start of each
# UTC month. A pure abuse ceiling until scans are gated behind an entitlement.
IDENTIFY_MONTHLY_LIMIT=40
DIAGNOSE_MONTHLY_LIMIT=80

# ── Eval-only candidate providers ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Everything below is scored by the evals/ harness and is NOT used by the app
# runtime. Leave blank unless running eval:* against that candidate. Issue
# project-scoped keys and set a prepaid balance + hard monthly limit as the
# cost cap.

# Pl@ntNet (identify only — no health endpoint). Free tier is 500
# identifications/day, which covers the comparison subsets outright.
# Key: https://my.plantnet.org/
PLANTNET_API_KEY=
# Optional flora project; defaults to `all` (world flora). Narrowing this
# hands Pl@ntNet a pre-filtered candidate space and biases the comparison.
PLANTNET_PROJECT=

# Claude. Deliberately not named after the vendor's default env var: CI's
# subscription-invariant grep hard-fails on that name anywhere in the repo.
CLAUDE_API_KEY=
# Optional override of the default model (claude-opus-5).
CLAUDE_MODEL=

# DeepSeek — placeholder, NOT yet usable. As of 2026-07-31 the public API is
# text-only: the chat-completions schema has no image content block and the
# open weights ship without vision, so there is nothing for an image adapter to
# call. Vision exists in their chat UI only. Re-check before wiring an adapter;
# v4-flash pricing undercuts gpt-4o-mini, so it is worth revisiting if it ships.
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=

# Postgres (server-only) — community waitlist + species knowledge base.
# Point at a POOLED endpoint in production (PgBouncer/pgcat in transaction
# mode); the app runs with prepare:false for exactly that reason. Apply
# migrations with `pnpm db:migrate`. Absent → the KB runs cache-only (dev).
DATABASE_URL=

# Redis (server-only) — scan rate limiting + usage log. Required by
# /api/identify and /api/diagnose (the client throws on first use if unset).
REDIS_URL=

# Structured log verbosity: debug | info | warn | error.
# Default: debug outside production, info in production.
LOG_LEVEL=
